component: lib/hosted-fixture-safety.mjs destructiveStatements() and auditSynthetic() preserved-table regex
defect: destructiveStatements() matches `delete\s+from\s+([a-z_][a-z0-9_]*)`: for `delete from public.t` it captures the SCHEMA (`public`) as the table, so every ownership rule (profile.ownership, e.g. financial_subsidy_claims→program_id) is blind to schema-qualified DELETEs: `subsidy[].present` reads false and the rule passes vacuously.
a QUOTED qualified DELETE (`delete from "public"."t" …`) is not matched at all: it is invisible to org-wide detection, to fixture scoping and to the synthetic run-scope rule.
the synthetic profile's preserved-table regex `(?:public\.)?${t}\b` misses `"public"."t"` for the same reason.

severity: the automated content guard can be satisfied by quoting identifiers; a fixture still needs registry pinning of exact bytes and review, so this is a defence-in-depth gap, not an exploit by itself. No currently registered fixture uses quoted or qualified deletes on an owned table (measured below).

proposed_fix.rule: match an optional ONLY, an optional (optionally quoted) schema qualifier and an optionally quoted table; report the bare table (lower-cased) and the schema separately; the preserved-table regex accepts the same shapes and ends on a non-identifier character instead of \b (\b fails after a closing quote)

proposed_fix_measured_on_copy.bypass_cases: all six cases above now resolve the real table; the four bypass/blind cases fail with the right reasons (org-wide delete; not constrained through program_id; writes retained data: person_health_facts; delete not scoped by org AND run)
proposed_fix_measured_on_copy.impact: no registered fixture changes verdict; ownership rules start applying to schema-qualified statements (financials_demo_tenant's qualified deletes, if any, are now held to program_id/agency_id — it still passes); a quoted or qualified write that dodged the guard is now refused. Callers that read `.table` get the bare table name; a new `.schema` field is additive.
